mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a P&L and a Balance Sheet?

acceptedAnswer.text: The P&L covers a period of time (did you make money over the month/year). The Balance Sheet is a single-moment snapshot of what you own and owe.

mainEntity.name: What is gross margin and why does it matter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gross profit as a percentage of revenue. It tells you whether your core offering is actually profitable, before overhead.

mainEntity.name: Does a profitable P&L mean I have money in the bank?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Profit is earned; cash is collected. A profitable business can still run short on cash.

mainEntity.name: How often should I review my P&L?

acceptedAnswer.text: Monthly, in comparison to prior periods and to budget — not once a year at tax time.
